newsitem.title: KENYA: Amnesty says action need for human rights in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says action need for human rights in Africa.

text.p: Stronger action is needed to counter human rights abuses in Africa, Amnesty International said in a statement on Monday to mark the anniversary of the adoption of the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights.
The charter, adopted by the Organisation of African Unity ten years ago, commits OAU member-states to protect and promote human rights.

But the last decade has been marked by an "increasing number of tragedies and the failure of governments to hold accountable those responsible", Amnesty said in a statement from its London headquarters.
"In Angola, Burundi, Nigeria and other African countries the Commission should make a determined effort to tackle the explosive human rights situation."
The statement coincided with the 20th session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights that starts on Monday in Mauritius.
Amnesty said the commission should immediately send a mission to Burundi, where "an already criticial human rgihts situation may be moving into a new and alarming phase."

A Hutu rebel war in Burundi has caused havoc in the country, which was taken over by the military in July. The war between the rebels and the Tutsi-dominated army has killed more than 150,000 people since October 1993.

Nigeria is also ruled by the military and there are complaints of human rights abuses. In Angola the opposition UNITA is under pressure to honour peace accords so the country does not fall back into civil war.

Amnesty also said the Mauritius meeting should look at the establishment of a permanent international criminal court to step in when national authorities are unwilling or unable perpetrators to justice.
"Over the past 10 years the Commission has adopted many resolutions -- but these have had little or no impact on the human rights situation in African countries," it said.
